meals.name: Creamy Pesto Chicken with Roasted Broccoli and Penne
meals.description: Pan-seared chicken breasts smothered in a creamy pesto sauce, served with al dente penne pasta and tender roasted broccoli, ready in about 40 minutes.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss broccoli florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

While pasta cooks, season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 165°F/74°C). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.

In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in chicken broth, pesto, and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer, then stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Return chicken to the skillet, coating it in the sauce. Serve immediately with the cooked penne pasta and roasted broccoli.

meals.name: Cheesy Ground Beef and Bean Enchilada Casserole
meals.description: Layers of seasoned ground beef, black beans, tortillas, and cheese baked in a savory enchilada sauce for a hearty meal, ready in about 45 minutes.

ingredients.name: Great Northern beans (or kidney beans), drained

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add ground beef to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, then drain any excess grease. Stir in chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in drained Great Northern beans and diced green chiles (undrained) into the ground beef mixture.

Spread 1/2 cup enchilada sauce on the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Layer with 6 corn tortillas, half of the ground beef mixture, and 1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese. Repeat layers: 6 tortillas, remaining beef mixture, and 1 cup enchilada sauce. Top with remaining 1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly, and the casserole is heated through. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

meals.name: Ginger-Soy Pork and Veggie Rice Bowls
meals.description: Quick-cooking pork tenderloin stir-fried with colorful vegetables in a savory ginger-soy sauce, served over fluffy rice, ready in about 35 minutes.
instructions: Cook white rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
While rice cooks, slice pork tenderloin into thin strips. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and cornstarch to create the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add pork strips and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until browned and mostly cooked through. Remove pork from the skillet and set aside.
Add broccoli florets, sliced carrots, and sliced red bell pepper to the same skillet. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.

Return pork to the skillet. Give the sauce a quick whisk, then pour it over the pork and vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats everything. Serve the pork and veggie mixture over the cooked rice, garnished with sliced green onions if desired.

meals.name: Slow Cooker Pulled BBQ Chicken Sandwiches
meals.description: Tender chicken thighs slow-cooked in a tangy BBQ sauce, shredded, and served on soft burger buns, perfect for a family dinner with minimal active effort, ready in about 4-6 hours (cook time).
instructions: Place chicken thighs in the bottom of a 6-quart (or larger) slow cooker.

In a medium bowl, whisk together BBQ sauce, chopped onion, garlic powder, paprika, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Pour the sauce mixture over the chicken, ensuring it is well coated.
Cover the slow cooker and cook on LOW for 4-6 hours, or until the chicken is very tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Carefully remove the chicken from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Shred the chicken using two forks, discarding any excess fat.
Return the shredded chicken to the slow cooker, stir it into the BBQ sauce, and let it simmer on LOW for another 15-30 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Serve the pulled BBQ chicken warm on burger buns, with coleslaw if desired.

meals.name: Speedy Tuna Melts on Texas Toast with Quick Tomato Basil Soup
meals.description: Classic cheesy tuna melts made with thick Texas toast, served alongside a warm bowl of ready-made tomato basil soup, on the table in under 30 minutes.
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the drained tuna, mayonnaise, finely chopped celery, finely diced red onion, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium heat. Butter one side of each slice of Texas toast. Place 4 slices, butter-side down, in the skillet.
Spread an even layer of the tuna mixture onto each of the 4 bread slices in the skillet. Top with 2 slices of cheese per sandwich. Place the remaining 4 slices of Texas toast (butter-side up) on top.
Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, or until the bread is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly.
While tuna melts cook, heat the can of Progresso Tomato Basil Soup according to package directions.
Serve the hot tuna melts immediately with bowls of warm tomato basil soup.

meals.name: Baked Salmon with Lemon-Dill Roasted Asparagus and Quinoa
meals.description: Flaky baked salmon fillets seasoned with lemon and dill, served with tender roasted asparagus and fluffy quinoa, a light yet satisfying meal ready in about 45 minutes.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Cook quinoa according to package directions.

Trim the woody ends off the asparagus spears. On a large baking sheet, toss asparagus with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half of the minced garlic, juice from 1/2 lemon, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.

Pat salmon fillets dry. Place them on the same baking sheet alongside the asparagus, leaving some space between. Drizzle salmon with 1 tablespoon olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with half of the chopped fresh dill and thin lemon slices from 1/2 lemon.
Bake for 12-18 minutes, depending on thickness, or until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork (internal temperature 145°F/63°C), and asparagus is tender-crisp.
While salmon bakes, prepare a dressing for the quinoa: whisk together the juice from the remaining lemon, remaining minced garlic, remaining fresh dill, 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Fluff the cooked quinoa and stir in the lemon-dill dressing. Serve the baked salmon and roasted asparagus immediately with the seasoned quinoa.

meals.name: Classic Shepherd's Pie (Beef)
meals.description: A comforting casserole with a savory ground beef and vegetable filling, topped with creamy mashed potatoes and baked until golden brown, ready in about 65 minutes.
instructions: Peel and chop potatoes into 1-inch cubes. Place in a large pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until very tender. Drain thoroughly.

While potatoes cook, preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet (or a Dutch oven) over medium heat. Add chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add ground beef to the skillet, breaking it apart. Cook until browned, then drain any excess grease. Stir in tomato paste and dried thyme, cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Stir in frozen peas. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mash the drained potatoes with 1/4 cup milk, 2 tablespoons butter, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy.

Spoon the mashed potatoes evenly over the beef and vegetable filling in the skillet. Use a fork to create decorative ridges on top. Sprinkle with shredded cheddar cheese. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbly. If desired, broil for the last 2-3 minutes for extra browning. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
